text:
ana: hey all, hit a weird case where a Retrofit call delivered onResponse after coroutine cancel. seems timing-sensitive and only on emulator/device API 33+.
joel: can you paste the wrapper you use? coroutines + Retrofit can be tricky.
ana: (typo) ana meant to say API 33 and 34 on Pixel images. sample below.
nana: repro code snippet: ```kotlin
suspend fun <T> Call<T>.awaitResponse(): Response<T> = suspendCancellableCoroutine { cont ->
  enqueue(object : Callback<T> {
    override fun onResponse(call: Call<T>, resp: Response<T>) {
      cont.resume(resp)
    }
    override fun onFailure(call: Call<T>, e: IOException) {
      cont.resumeWithException(e)
    }
  })
  cont.invokeOnCancellation { cancel() }
}
```
joel: small bug: inside onResponse you should check cont.isActive before resume. if cancel raced, resume might still run. but suspendCancellableCoroutine.invokeOnCancellation calling cancel() should stop the call, right?
tasha: right — but cancel() may not prevent the callback being posted to the executor if response already parsed. I've seen a race where dispatcher threads enqueue the callback onto the callbackExecutor after network finishes but before cancel propagates.
nana: logs from Pixel 7 API 33 repro: ```
D/App: start await
D/OkHttp: request started
D/App: cancel invoked
D/OkHttp: response parsed 200
D/App: onResponse delivered - body size=512
D/App: coroutine cancelled exception in caller
```
joel: does your wrapper create multiple Call instances (like cloning) or store the Call instance correctly? clone() returns a fresh Call and cancel has to be called on the same instance.
nana: good catch — my service function did `val c = api.getX().clone()` in one branch and `invokeOnCancellation { c.cancel() }` in another — could be a mismatch. repro updated to simpler path though and still flaky.
tasha: try two quick changes: 1) check cont.isActive before resume (fast guard), 2) set client.dispatcher().maxRequests = 2 in local repro to increase contention and see if behavior changes.
joel: also try upgrading Retrofit to 2.9.0 -> 2.9.3 (if available) and OkHttp 4.11.0 -> 4.11.1 (patch) — there were fixes around callback executor ordering recently.
nana: CI run queued: https://ci.redwood/repro/122 - emulator matrix api 29/30/33/34. ci-bot: started run 122 (emulator api 29,30,33,34)
ci-bot: run 122: repro flaky on api 33 and 34, not on 29/30.
joel: that smells like a platform scheduler change vs okhttp runtime. can you try setting callbackExecutor to same as caller to avoid extra handoff? ```java
new Retrofit.Builder()
 .callbackExecutor(Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor())
```
tasha: also try client.dispatcher().executorService().shutdown() after test to force flush in unit tests — not great for prod.
nana: added cont.isActive guard and switched to coroutine adapter wrapper we maintain in SDK that cancels underlying call on coroutine cancel. flaky deliveries dropped in my local runs. pushing PR with notes for SDK docs: always guard callback resume with coroutine active check and prefer suspend wrapper that cancels underlying call.
joel: open a small devex doc with recommended pattern + sample code? we should include clone/call lifetime gotchas.
nana: will do. filing follow-up ticket ENG-RUNTIME-798 to investigate whether OkHttp should avoid dispatching callbacks after cancel on the same Call instance. attaching repro: https://paste.example/repro-2179990001
ci-bot: run 122 finished: 3/8 flakes reproduced on api 33 images.
nana: thanks y'all — I'll leave the PR draft and ticket link in the repo and update here. :seedling:
